title: The goat that walked home
prose: One of the drovers tells about a goat sold at a market three days' walk away, that turned up at the fold a week later with the buyer's rope still on it. They kept the rope, she says, and the goat, and gave the buyer a better one. He came to visit it after.

choices.label: Ask if it still walks home
choices.line: Every time, she says, which is why nobody buys from them twice. She does not seem to think this is a problem.

choices.label: Laugh
choices.line: You laugh, and she looks pleased, as if the story has done what it is for.

notes: A fireside story for a night slept beside a camp of drovers (Roads and Hands, phase 5). Shared by every map, as the owner's four camp kinds are. Drafted for the owner to rewrite or approve.
